match.reason: The closest bank point, phys-mass-energy, covers E=mc², mass change and nuclear energy, but it never states total energy as γmc² or splits it into rest energy plus kinetic energy, which is the new point's core idea.

draft.title: Mass and energy in relativity
card: An object's total energy is E = γmc². Here m is its rest mass, c is the speed of light, and γ is the Lorentz factor, which is 1 at rest and grows as speed rises.
At rest, γ = 1 and the energy is the rest energy, E = mc². Total energy = rest energy + kinetic energy, so kinetic energy = (γ - 1)mc².
Mass and energy can be converted. In the Sun, hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium, and the products have slightly less mass than the starting nuclei. The lost mass is released as energy.
In annihilation, a particle and its antiparticle meet and their whole rest mass becomes energy, usually as photons. The energy released is the rest energy of both particles.
draft.remember: Total energy is γmc²: rest energy mc² plus kinetic energy. Lost mass becomes released energy.

a.q: An electron is moving at high speed. Which expression gives its kinetic energy?
a.why: Kinetic energy is total energy minus rest energy, so γmc² - mc² = (γ - 1)mc². The total energy γmc² is tempting, but it also includes the rest energy.
a.clue: Take the rest energy away from the total energy.

b.q: In a lab, an electron and its antiparticle meet at rest and annihilate. What is the total energy released?
opts: The rest energy of both particles, 2mc²
The rest energy of one particle, mc²
Only the kinetic energy of both particles
Nothing, because mass is always conserved separately
b.why: All the rest mass of both particles becomes energy, so the energy is mc² + mc² = 2mc². Counting only one particle is tempting, but both particles lose their mass.
b.clue: Count the rest energy of each particle that disappears.

b.best: The rest energy of both particles, 2mc²
